```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
Life_Expectancy_Data <- read.csv("Life-Expectancy-Data-Updated.csv")

```

# Checking data
First, we want to see the structure of our data. What variables do we have, for which countries, etc. 
Then we will check if the data has any empty, missing or weird entries. 

## Data structure
What columns do we have? How many rows?
```{r}
colnames(Life_Expectancy_Data)

paste(nrow(Life_Expectancy_Data), "rows")
```
There are 21 columns and 2864 rows. 
Important to note for some columns: 
* Hepatitis B, Measles, Polio and Diphteria show % of *vaccination* coverage, not incidence
Further information on what these columns represent is explained on the Kaggle page under Data sources: 
[Kaggle data sources](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/lashagoch/life-expectancy-who-updated/data).

What is the structure in the rows?
For example, how many countries are there? How many years?
```{r}
print(paste(length(unique(Life_Expectancy_Data$Country)), "countries"))
print(paste(length(unique(Life_Expectancy_Data$Year)), "years"))
```
Are all countries present for each year?
```{r}
print("Is the number of obervations equal to the number of countries times number of years?")
length(unique(Life_Expectancy_Data$Country)) * length(unique(Life_Expectancy_Data$Year)) == nrow(Life_Expectancy_Data)

print("How many countries are present for all 16 years?")
sum(table(Life_Expectancy_Data$Country) == 16)
```



```{r column info}
str(Life_Expectancy_Data)
#  columns contain character data, 8 contain integer data,
# and 12 contain numeric data.
summary(Life_Expectancy_Data)
#Several columns contain missing values (NA),
# particularly Population, Hepatitis.B and GDP.
```

```{r row info} 
# how many countries
length(unique(Life_Expectancy_Data$Country))
length(unique(Life_Expectancy_Data$Country[Life_Expectancy_Data$Status == "Developing"]))
length(unique(Life_Expectancy_Data$Country[Life_Expectancy_Data$Status == "Developed"]))
# what years included?
range(Life_Expectancy_Data$Year)

```

```{r}
table(Life_Expectancy_Data$Year)
#each year has an equal amount of countries, good!
```


```{r data info}
# how many NAs?
sum(is.na(Life_Expectancy_Data))
sum(Life_Expectancy_Data == "")
#these are not present!

# structure of the data
```
Here I will make a function to easily plot any variable over time for *one* country:
```{r}
var_over_time = function(var, country){
  plot(x = Life_Expectancy_Data[Life_Expectancy_Data$Country == country, "Year"],
       y = Life_Expectancy_Data[Life_Expectancy_Data$Country == country, var],
       main = paste(var, "over time for", country),
       xlab = "Time (years)",
       ylab = var
       )
}

var_over_time("Under_five_deaths", "Kenya")
```
